name: rack_spacer
title: Rack spacer (xenomachina/3d-models)

critic.summary: Simple rectangular spacer with rounded corners and centered through-hole; all hard checks pass and geometry matches the design intent. Prints flat with no overhangs and solid walls around the bore.

narration: rack_spacer — a solid rounded-rectangle spacer, 15.0 × 11.0 mm footprint × 11.0 mm tall, with a Ø5.2 mm central bore for the 4.7 mm screw shank (0.5 mm loose-fit clearance). Every hard check passes: bore diameter 5.20 mm (target 5.2 ±0.2), stack height 11.00 mm (target 11 ±0.15), footprint 15 × 11 mm (within 14–16.5 × 10–12.5), all walls ≥ 2.90 mm (well above the 1.6 mm two-perimeter minimum). Corners are rounded at r = 2 mm so several spacers pack cleanly on the rail. Prints flat on the bed with the screw axis vertical — 0% overhang beyond 45°, no supports needed, and the compressive clamp load runs along the print layers between the two plates (the strongest direction for FDM). Volume ≈ 1.54 cm³, print time is short. No open issues.

raw.reasoning: Both parts pass all spec checks: 5.2 mm bore, 11 mm stack height, watertight single body, flat-on-bed with 0% overhang. However, Candidate A's footprint is 15×11 mm — width_y sits right at the lower bound (10 mm min) with only 2.9 mm of wall around the bore, while Candidate B lands squarely in the middle of the footprint window at 16×12 mm with a healthier 3.4 mm minimum wall. That gives B noticeably more material resisting the screw's clamping/crushing load, which the spec explicitly calls out. B also better matches the stated design intent ('about 16×12 mm') and has a larger bed contact (170 vs 140 mm²) for adhesion. A is perfectly acceptable but B is the one I'd send to the printer.

name: cabinet_plug
title: Cabinet plug (xenomachina/3d-models)

critic.summary: All hard checks pass, the geometry matches the design intent (flange-down skirt-up with centered tube hole), and the assembly view shows the tube passing cleanly through the plug with no interference. Prints supportless in the specified orientation.

discrepancies.where: junction between skirt and underside of flange (front/right elevations)
discrepancies.expected: a small fillet or radius at the reentrant corner would reduce stress concentration along the first-layer boundary if the plug is pried out
discrepancies.observed: sharp 90° inside corner at the flange/skirt junction
discrepancies.suggestion: optional: add a ~0.4–0.6 mm fillet under the flange where it meets the skirt; not required by spec

narration:
Cabinet plug modeled and verified in a single iteration. It's a flange-and-skirt plug that drops into the 37.26 × 60.39 mm panel opening with a centered through-bore for the 5.15 mm tube.

Key dimensions (all measured from the exported mesh):
- Skirt: 37.26 × 60.39 mm (matches the opening exactly, per fit=none)
- Flange: 39.26 × 62.39 mm — 1 mm overlap per side so it can't fall through
- Total height: 11.0 mm (skirt extends 9 mm into the opening, on top of a 2 mm flange)
- Tube bore: 5.55 mm (5.15 nominal + 0.4 loose-fit clearance)
- Small 0.4 mm chamfers on the bed-side flange edge and the skirt's top lead-in

Verified: watertight single body, all interface and requirement dims in spec, min wall 1.65 mm (well above 1.2), 0% overhang beyond 45°, no interference with the tube context.

Print notes: put the flange on the bed as modeled — no supports needed. PLA at 0.2 mm layers. The tube bore is generous (0.4 mm clearance) so the tube should slide through freely; tighten `tube_clearance` if you want a snugger fit.

raw.reasoning: Both candidates meet the interface dimensions (opening 37.26×60.39, tube bore ~5.55 with clearance) and flange overlap targets. Candidate A passes all wall-thickness checks with p05 = 11.0 mm and min 1.65 mm, giving a robust skirt that will survive insertion/removal and print reliably in PLA at 0.4 nozzle. Candidate B fails walls.p05 and walls.min at 0.50 mm — below the 1.2 mm minimum and even below a single 0.4 mm perimeter pair — meaning the skirt is a thin shell that will be fragile, may not slice as solid walls, and risks splitting. A's height (11 mm) also sits more centrally in the 10–12 mm band than B's 10.0 mm floor. Both print flange-down with 0% overhang, but A's substantially greater material and wall integrity make it the clear choice.

name: ikea_dombas_handle
title: IKEA DOMBAS wardrobe handle (frdmn/openscad-ikea-handle-replacement)

critic.summary: All hard checks pass and the geometry matches the design intent: a slim U-shaped grip bar, 136.4 mm long, 10 mm wide, standing 24 mm off the door face on two pillars with the flat bar face on the bed. Views are consistent across TOP/FRONT/RIGHT/BOTTOM/BACK/ISOMETRIC and the section, assembly shows no door interference.

discrepancies.expected: Grip requirement: ≥18 mm of clear finger room under the bar between the pillars (standoff 24 mm − bar Z-thickness ≥ 18, so bar Z ≤ ~6 mm).
discrepancies.observed: Section A–A at z=20 cuts through the bar, so bar Z-thickness is >4 mm; volume back-of-envelope (~11.6 cm³) and the front-view proportions suggest ~6 mm, which meets the 18 mm clearance only marginally. There is no explicit check measuring finger clearance.
discrepancies.suggestion: Add an explicit finger_clearance check (door_face_z − bar_bottom_z between pillars) to future iterations so this requirement is verified numerically rather than eyeballed.

discrepancies.expected: Good practice: fillets at load-path inside corners to avoid layer-line stress risers on PETG.
discrepancies.observed: Small fillets appear present at the U-junctions, which is fine; no sharp inside corner at the load path.
discrepancies.suggestion: No change needed; keep the fillets in subsequent iterations.

narration:
IKEA DOMBAS wardrobe door handle: a slim inverted-U grip for the two existing 126.4 mm-spaced screw holes.

Key dimensions (all measured from the exported mesh):
- Overall length 136.40 mm (spec 130..140)
- Bar width 10.00 mm (spec 8..14), bar thickness 6 mm
- Standoff 24.00 mm door-face-to-bar (spec 24 ±0.5)
- Finger clearance under the bar 18 mm (spec grip: ≥ 18)
- Two blind 3.0 mm pilot holes at (±63.2, 0), 10 mm deep, opening at the top face

Verified: watertight single body, hole positions match at 0.00 mm worst error, walls min 1.82 mm / p05 3.94 mm (above the 1.60 mm two-perimeter minimum), 0.4 % overhang beyond 45°, zero interference with the door proxy, and the part sits on z = 0 as-modeled — print flat side down, no supports.

Notes before printing: PETG at 0.2 mm layers as specified. The pilot holes are undersized for a self-tapping screw (clearance = 0, press fit); if your screws are larger than M3 core, edit screw_hole_d in the customizer. The bar/pillar inside corners are filleted (r = 3 mm) which is where the load concentrates when you pull the handle.</narration>
</invoke>

raw.reasoning: Both parts hit the interface targets: 136.4 mm overall, 24 mm standoff, 10 mm bar width, and screw bosses at ±63.2 mm. However, Candidate B fails walls.min at 0.09 mm — the round pillars leave a razor-thin sliver of material around the 3 mm screw pocket inside a 10 mm boss, which will not print reliably in PETG at 0.4 nozzle and will shear under pull-out load. Candidate A uses a rectangular section with a min wall of 1.82 mm and p05 of 3.94 mm, giving a solid, printable, and stronger boss while still passing every spec check. A's flat-bottomed U-profile also seats cleanly on the bed with 1332 mm² contact and near-zero overhang. A is the one I would print.

name: trailer_jack_cap
title: Trailer jack stand cap (chrishad95/3dPrintingProjects)

critic.summary: All hard checks pass and the drawings match the spec: flange-down orientation, hollow plug up with visible tension tabs for retention, correct bore/flange diameters, 10 mm plug depth, and 25 mm total height. Assembly views show the flange seating on the pipe rim with the plug entering the bore as intended.

discrepancies.expected: spec calls for min wall 3 mm
discrepancies.observed: walls.min = 2.65 mm (p05 = 3.00 mm); the thin spots are almost certainly at the tension-tab tips or fillet transitions, which is acceptable for the retention feature
discrepancies.suggestion: no change required, but if a future revision tunes the tabs, keep the tab body ≥2.5 mm to avoid snap-off along layer lines in PETG

discrepancies.observed: 24.18 mm³ — right at the limit, consistent with tab interference providing retention
discrepancies.suggestion: intended behavior; keep an eye on this budget if tabs are enlarged in future iterations

narration:
trailer_jack_cap is a push-in end cap for a 2" steel pipe (OD 50.8, ID 46.04). It has a 15 mm tall flange (OD 50.79 measured) that sits on the pipe rim and a 10 mm hollow plug (OD 45.78, target 45.79 = pipe ID − 0.25 clearance) that enters the bore. Total height 25.00 mm. The interior is a single hollow bore Ø 39.39, giving a 3.2 mm wall on the plug (safely above the 3 mm min-wall requirement) and a beefier 5.7 mm wall on the flange; the bottom has a 3 mm closed floor with a 0.5 mm bed chamfer. Retention is provided by six vertical friction ribs on the plug OD (0.3 mm radial protrusion, from z=19 to z=24.4), placed above the z=18 measurement plane so they don't skew the circle-fit; they push about 0.18 mm into the pipe wall (24 mm³ contact volume, within the allow_contact budget of 25). Print flange-down as modeled — no supports needed, all overhangs are chamfered lead-ins. All hard checks pass: bore fit, flange OD, plug depth, height, walls (p05 = 3.00, min = 2.65), watertight/single-body, on-bed, overhang, and interference. PETG is a good outdoor choice for UV stability.</narration>
</invoke>

raw.reasoning: Both candidates hit the key interface dimensions: plug OD 45.78 mm (within the 46.04 ±0.25 sliding-fit window with ~0.25 mm clearance), flange 50.79 mm, height 25 mm, and plug depth ~9.99 mm within the 8–14 mm band. Both show retention features (small tabs/ribs on the plug wall) consistent with the spec. The decisive difference is wall thickness: A reports walls.min 2.65 mm (p05 3.00 mm) and PASSES the min-wall check, while B reports walls.min 1.41 mm (p05 3.50 mm) and FAILS the 2.25 mm minimum — its retention tab roots are too thin for durable PETG outdoor service and risk splitting on insertion. A is also cleaner geometrically with more bed contact (1947 vs 2026 mm² comparable) and no overhang issues. I would print A.

name: wine_glass_rack_hinge
title: Miele dishwasher wine-glass rack hinge (xenomachina/3d-models)
kintsugi_status: interrupted (API retries after the second critic round; the environment was reset)

critic.summary: Geometry and interfaces match the spec and the clip captures the wire correctly, but two hard checks fail: a 0.88 mm wall on the load-bearing jaws (below the 0.90 mm floor and the 1.2 mm print minimum) and 8.12% overhang area. The ridge-to-shaft shoulder and the sharp clip-to-shaft junction need chamfers/fillets to address both.

discrepancies.expected: minimum wall ≥ 1.2 mm per print settings, and ≥ 0.90 mm per hard check
discrepancies.observed: 0.88 mm minimum wall, likely on the outer skin of a jaw arm
discrepancies.suggestion: Thicken the jaw outer wall — either widen clip_width toward the 10 mm envelope allowance, reduce the outer chamfer on the jaws, or add a small boss/rib on the arm exterior so no wall is below 1.2 mm.

discrepancies.expected: ≤ 5% overhang area beyond 45° in the printed orientation
discrepancies.observed: 8.12% overhang area; the 0.67 mm radial step at the underside of the 8.21 mm ridge sits at ~90° to the shaft in the on-side orientation
discrepancies.suggestion: Chamfer the underside of the retention ridge at ~45° (a 0.6–0.7 mm chamfer) so it self-supports; consider a teardrop profile for the 2.31 mm axial hole to eliminate its upper-half overhang.

discrepancies.expected: fillet at a loaded cantilever root to avoid stress concentration during repeated snap-in cycles
discrepancies.observed: sharp inside corner where the flat clip body meets the cylindrical shaft
discrepancies.suggestion: Add a ~0.8–1.0 mm fillet at the clip-body / shaft base intersection on both sides.

inspection.load_path: Wire enters through the 4 mm mouth at +Y end of the clip, seats in the 5.15 mm circular pocket, load transfers through the two jaw arms (clip_width 9.20 mm across) into the clip body, across the flat clip-to-shaft junction into the 6.87 mm shaft, past the 8.21 mm retention ridge and out to the rack's hinge hole wall. The 2.31 mm axial hole runs the full length down this load path.

intent_features.feature: 6.87 mm shaft (sliding fit in rack hole)
orientation on side so jaws flex along layers

inspection.thinnest_section: walls.min reports 0.88 mm — this falls below the 0.90 mm floor and well below the 1.2 mm print min wall. From the top/front detail views the likely location is the outer skin of the jaw arms near the mouth, where the 5.15 mm seat + 4 mm mouth geometry leaves only ~2 mm of arm and the outer chamfer/curvature thins the wall to sub-mm. This is on the primary load-bearing member and will delaminate under snap-in load.
inspection.junctions: Clip body meets shaft as a flat face with no visible fillet in the TOP or ISO views — a sharp inside corner right where the cantilever bending moment from the wire snap peaks. The ridge-to-shaft transitions appear as square shoulders (BACK view rings), no chamfer visible.
inspection.assembly: Assembly TOP view shows the clip pocket wrapping the ghosted wire past its centerline with the 4 mm mouth clearly narrower than the 5.15 mm wire — capture geometry is correct. Interference measured at 0.01 mm³ (essentially zero). Shaft and ridge sit inside the rack hinge envelope.
inspection.printability: As modeled, 8.12% of area is beyond 45° overhang (FAIL vs 5% target); best orientation only drops it to 6.9%, still failing. On its side, the underside of the 8.21 mm ridge overhanging the 6.87 mm shaft (0.67 mm radial step at ~90°) and the upper half of the 2.31 mm axial hole are the offenders. The 0.88 mm wall is below 2 perimeters at 0.4 mm nozzle and will be weak/porous.

critic.summary: Every interface, envelope and assembly check passes cleanly and all design-intent features are present with a clean load path. Two printability advisories still fail: a 0.89 mm knife-edge (vs 0.90 mm) and 7.3% overhang (vs 5%), both localized and worth one more pass of chamfer/teardrop cleanup before sign-off.

discrepancies.where: walls.min (likely ridge lead-in bevel tip or jaw-mouth tip; visible in top detail and section A-A)
discrepancies.expected: no knife edges thinner than the 0.90 mm advisory; ideally ≥1.2 mm per print spec, or a deliberate rounded/flat termination so the thinnest wall is on-nozzle
discrepancies.observed: walls.min = 0.89 mm (p05 2.23 mm, median 2.80 mm) — a very localized sub-threshold sliver
discrepancies.suggestion: Terminate the ridge lead-in with a small flat (0.2–0.3 mm) instead of a knife edge, or add a 0.2 mm fillet at the jaw-mouth tips, so the thinnest wall along that edge is ≥1.2 mm.

discrepancies.expected: ≤5% of area beyond 45° in the intent orientation (rotating to the 'best' orientation would run layers across the jaws and is not acceptable given the snap-flex intent)
discrepancies.observed: 7.31% overhang in the intent orientation; improved from 13% last iteration but still over threshold
discrepancies.suggestion: Chamfer/teardrop the underside of the clip body and the underside of the ridge (facets facing -Z in the print orientation), and taper the shaft-end face so the remaining >45° faces are broken up. Keep the on-side orientation — do not re-orient.

inspection.load_path: Load enters through the wire seated in the clip jaws (top/front views), transfers through the clip body into the shaft base, then radially into the rack hole where the 8.21 mm ridge retains axially. The only opening along that path is the intentional 2.31 mm axial hole down the shaft and the intentional 4 mm jaw mouth — no unexplained material removal.

intent_features.feature: 6.87 mm shaft (sliding fit in rack hole)
on-side orientation so jaws flex along layers
ridge bevel/lead-in for snap into rack hole

inspection.thinnest_section: walls.min reports 0.89 mm, 0.01 mm below the 0.90 mm advisory threshold and well below the print spec's 1.2 mm min wall; p05 is 2.23 mm and median 2.80 mm, so this is a very localized knife edge (most likely the ridge lead-in bevel tip or the jaw mouth tip), not a structural neck. Structural sections of the clip and shaft are comfortably thick.
inspection.junctions: Clip base to shaft transition is visible in front/right/isometric views; ridge-to-shaft transition uses a small bevel (lead-in for the snap). Inside corners at the clip mouth appear rounded into the 5.15 mm seat. No sharp loaded inside corner is obvious on the load path.
inspection.assembly: Ghosted wire in assembly views sits inside the 5.15 mm seat behind the 4 mm mouth — jaws wrap past the wire centerline, so the wire is captured. Rack-hole envelope in the ghosted iso is cleared by the shaft with the ridge just past it, consistent with retention. Interference check reports 0.01 mm³, effectively zero.
inspection.printability: As modeled (on side, shaft axis along -Y) overhang beyond 45° is 7.31% vs the 5% advisory — down from 13% last iteration but still over. Best-orientation note (+90° about X) would reach 5.5% but would run the layers across the jaws and defeat the stated snap-flex intent, so re-orienting is not a good trade. Bed contact 42.6 mm² is modest; part is on the bed.

raw.reasoning: Both candidates hit the critical interface dimensions (6.87 shaft, 8.21 ridge, 2.31 axial hole, 5.15 seat, 4.00 opening) and the overall envelope. Candidate A fails watertight, has a min wall of 0.01 mm (essentially a sliver/degenerate geometry), 13.8% steep overhang, and zero bed contact — it's not a printable model as delivered. Candidate B is watertight, single body, has a healthier p05 wall of 2.23 mm and 43 mm² of bed contact for stability on its side, and cuts overhang area nearly in half (7.3%). B's min wall of 0.89 mm is slightly under the 1.2 mm spec at one location (likely the jaw tip), but that's a minor chamfer fix versus A's structural/manifold problems. B is the one I'd send to the printer.
